title: Controlled vs uncontrolled inputs
objectives: Wire a controlled input by pairing value from state with an onChange that writes e.target.value
Predict what an input with value but no onChange does: a frozen field plus a React warning
Choose an uncontrolled input (defaultValue plus a ref) when you only need the value on submit
Spot the uncontrolled-to-controlled warning and fix it by keeping value defined from the first render
Show data that loads after the first render in an editable field: render the form once it's loaded, or remount it with a key

sources.title: React docs: Manipulating the DOM with Refs
React docs: Preserving and Resetting State

questions.prompt: What makes an <input> a controlled component in React?

options.text: Its value comes from state via `value`, and `onChange` writes every change back to state
It has an `onChange` handler, regardless of `value`

questions.explanation: Controlled = React state owns the value. You pass the current value in with `value` and push every keystroke back to state with `onChange`. The two are a pair: `value` alone (no `onChange`) makes the field read-only and triggers a warning; `onChange` alone without `value` is just an uncontrolled input with a listener.

questions.prompt: You render `<input value={query} />` with no `onChange`. What happens when the user types?

options.text: Nothing changes on screen and React warns you supplied `value` without `onChange`
It updates normally — `value` tracks the DOM automatically
The input updates but `query` stays stale

questions.explanation: With `value` set to a state variable that never changes, React reverts the input to that fixed value after every keystroke, so the field appears frozen (effectively read-only). React logs that you provided `value` without `onChange` and suggests `defaultValue` or `readOnly`. Add `onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)}` to make it controlled.

questions.prompt: When is an uncontrolled input (`defaultValue` + a ref) a reasonable choice?

options.text: When you only need the value at a single moment (e.g. on submit) and don't need to react to each keystroke
When you want to validate or filter as the user types
Never — every input should be controlled

questions.explanation: Uncontrolled inputs let the DOM own the value; you read it from a ref on demand. That's a fine fit when you only care about the final value (form submit), for file inputs (which are always uncontrolled), or to avoid a re-render per keystroke. If you need to react as the user types — live filtering, validation, enabling a button — go controlled.

questions.prompt: `NameForm` seeds `const [name, setName] = useState(initialName)` and binds the input to `name`. The parent renders `<NameForm initialName={user?.name ?? ""} />` while `user` is loading, and again once it arrives. What does the field show, and what's the fix?

options.text: It stays empty: `useState` reads its argument only on the first render. Render `NameForm` only once `user` has loaded, or give it `key={user?.id}` so it remounts with the name
It shows the loaded name: `useState` picks up its new argument when the prop changes
It stays empty; fix it with `useEffect(() => setName(initialName))` so state always follows the prop
It stays empty; fix it with `useState(initialName ?? "")` so the value is never undefined

questions.explanation: react.dev: `useState`'s initial value "is ignored after the initial render". The first render saw `""`, so `name` stays `""` when the user arrives. Don't copy the prop in later — a dependency-less sync effect overwrites every keystroke on the next render. Instead, make the form start *after* the data exists: `{user ? <NameForm initialName={user.name} /> : <Spinner />}`, or change its `key` when the data arrives so React discards the old state and runs `useState` again. `?? ""` keeps an input controlled; it does nothing to make a later value appear (here `initialName` is already a string).

prompts.prompt: Wire up a controlled text input bound to the `query` state.
prompts.explanation: A controlled input pairs `value={query}` with `onChange`, and the new text lives at `e.target.value`. Together they keep React state as the single source of truth for the field.

prompts.prompt: `user` is `{}` until the fetch resolves. Keep this input controlled from the very first render.
prompts.explanation: While `user.name` is `undefined`, `value={undefined}` means "no value", so the input starts uncontrolled; when the name arrives it becomes controlled and React warns. Coalescing to `""` — react.dev's own fix, `value={someValue ?? ''}` — keeps `value` a string from the first render. `??` replaces only `null`/`undefined`; `||` also replaces other falsy values, which is the same for a string but would turn a number input's `0` into an empty field.

code: // user is {} until the fetch resolves, then { name: "Ada" }
snippets.question: What does React log when the fetch resolves?
snippets.answer: A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled.
acceptable: changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled
snippets.explanation: On the first render `user.name` is undefined, and `value={undefined}` counts as no value at all, so React treats the input as uncontrolled. When the data arrives, `value` becomes `"Ada"` and the input switches to controlled — React logs "A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled" (it shows "Ada", but an input mustn't switch modes during its life). Fix: `value={user.name ?? ""}`.

code: // user is {} until the fetch resolves, then { name: "Ada" }
// The fetch resolves. Then the user types "x".
snippets.question: What does the input show after the fetch resolves, and when does React log the uncontrolled-to-controlled warning?
snippets.answer: It stays empty after the fetch (no warning yet); the warning fires on the first keystroke
acceptable: empty, then the warning on the first keystroke
stays empty; warns when the user types
snippets.explanation: `useState(user.name)` reads `user.name` once, on the first render, when it's undefined; react.dev says the initial value is ignored after that. So when the fetch resolves, `name` is still undefined — the field stays empty and nothing switches, so no warning. Typing calls `setName("x")`, `value` goes from undefined to a string, and *that* render logs the warning. Writing `useState(user.name ?? "")` silences the warning but still never shows "Ada". To edit loaded data, render the field once the data exists or remount it with a `key`.
